author: WP16
summary: Alpha.1-era explanation of how CNA consumes modular sharp-runtime: directories vs components, include vs link closure, standalone vs embedded selection, the sibling contract, cna_link_sharp_runtime, component tests and upgrade rules. At TARGET CNA passes its closure in SHARP_RUNTIME_COMPONENTS, so the embedded build is no longer All; the closure has 13(+1) components and 21 call sites. The CNA-side seam was already on the third-party-dependencies page; the registry mechanics, per-module table and upgrade rules are on the new components page.

concepts.section: Components and CNA Integration
concepts.text: The 2026-08-10 modular merge (f827a6c5) replaced sharp-runtime's one-archive build; descriptions based on the monolith can be coherent yet wrong for the pair, and the revision read now is 422 commits later.

concepts.section: Components and CNA Integration
concepts.text: The consumption question has two layers: which target supplies an included header, and how that target reaches the final program; component availability and a target's declared link interface are different questions.

concepts.section: Directories, components, and targets are different counts
concepts.text: Module directories and registered component names differ: at 41b918c9 44 directories register 47 names (33 static, 13 interface, 1 alias).

concepts.section: Directories, components, and targets are different counts
concepts.text: Core and Collections are compatibility umbrellas and Xml.XPath is an alias of Xml; other names are families such as Core.Base, Collections.Core, IO, Text.Json, Threading.Tasks, Net.WebSockets.

concepts.section: Directories, components, and targets are different counts
concepts.text: Consumers link the namespaced form SharpRuntime::<Component>, never an archive file name.

concepts.section: Directories, components, and targets are different counts
concepts.text: Module CMake files call sharp_runtime_register_module instead of add_library; the registry globs sources and tests, enforces kind rules and materialises targets when enabled.

concepts.section: Directories, components, and targets are different counts
concepts.text: A source-partition validator and an empty dependency allowlist make ownership leaks visible before compilation.

concepts.section: Directories, components, and targets are different counts
concepts.text: The generated component catalogue measures direct production dependency edges: 108 at 41b918c9, a third number distinct from directories and names.

concepts.section: Header names predict location, not the link closure
concepts.text: There is no SharpRuntime.hpp; System/IO/MemoryStream.hpp belongs to the IO component, whose public dependencies propagate, so a consumer names its direct component.

concepts.section: Header names predict location, not the link closure
concepts.text: CNA's direct includes (81 at TARGET) map to 14 owning components; SharpRuntimeHelper.hpp and Prop.hpp belong to Core.Base while other headers such as SHA256 bring other components.

target.evidence: modules/*/include, modules/*/src at 009d40f5 mapped to sharp-runtime@41b918c9 modules

concepts.section: Standalone selection and embedded selection differ
concepts.text: As the top-level project sharp-runtime exposes SHARP_RUNTIME_COMPONENTS defaulting to All, and the legacy SHARP_RUNTIME interface exists only for the All selection.

concepts.section: Standalone selection and embedded selection differ
concepts.text: Embedded, CNA now sets SHARP_RUNTIME_COMPONENTS to its closure before add_subdirectory, so only the closure and its dependencies are configured and SharpRuntime::All never exists.
concepts.note: Bible: embedded selection falls through to All and every component is compiled.

concepts.section: Standalone selection and embedded selection differ
concepts.text: CNA's narrow lists both document link boundaries and, at this snapshot, limit what is configured and compiled; the earlier 'not a pruning mechanism' reading is outdated.
tokens: the narrow closure also limits what is configured and compiled

concepts.section: CNA's sibling contract
concepts.text: sharp-runtime is CNA's one unconditional sibling; CNA forces SHARP_RUNTIME_BUILD_TESTS off so the sibling's test executables never join a CNA build.

concepts.section: CNA's sibling contract
concepts.text: CNA_SHARP_RUNTIME_ROOT defaults to ../sharp-runtime; a missing CMakeLists.txt is a fatal configure error with a clone remedy; there is no submodule, vendored copy or FetchContent fallback.

concepts.section: CNA's sibling contract
concepts.text: SharpRuntimeConsumption.cmake recognises a modular checkout (SharpRuntime::Core.Base exists) or falls back to the monolithic SHARP_RUNTIME archive for old checkouts.

concepts.section: CNA's sibling contract
concepts.text: Shape detection tests a target, not a version string, so CNA does not have to learn the sibling's release numbering.
tokens: not by reading a version string

concepts.section: The linking helper makes closures explicit
concepts.text: cna_link_sharp_runtime(target visibility [components]) prefixes SharpRuntime:: on a modular checkout, falls back to the archive on a monolithic one and uses the default closure when no names are given.
tokens: with no names it uses the default closure

concepts.section: The linking helper makes closures explicit
concepts.text: CNA's default closure is Core.Base, IO, Collections.Core, Collections.ObjectModel, Runtime, Threading, Text, Globalization, ComponentModel, Storage, Security.Cryptography, Xml and Resources, plus Xml.Serialization off Windows.

concepts.section: The linking helper makes closures explicit
concepts.text: The closure is not transitive: Uri, TimeZone and Buffers arrive through public edges and are deliberately not repeated, which would duplicate the sibling's registry.

concepts.section: The linking helper makes closures explicit
concepts.text: Nineteen CNA module CMake files make 21 explicit calls (math Core.Base; input Core.Base+Collections.Core; graphics Core.Base, IO, Collections.Core, Text; net adds Runtime, Threading; gamer services adds Globalization); every renderer family target uses the default closure.
concepts.note: Bible: eighteen call sites, input only Core.Base, one renderer aggregation target.

concepts.section: The linking helper makes closures explicit
concepts.text: The helper lets current modules state precise boundaries while keeping a controlled path to old checkouts; the narrow declaration is the durable contract.
tokens: the durable part of the contract

concepts.section: Tests enforce component ownership
concepts.text: Each component with tests gets SharpRuntimeTests_<component>, linked only to its component, gtest_main and declared test-only dependencies, with the component name as discovery prefix.

concepts.section: Tests enforce component ownership
concepts.text: Four module directories have no component tests at 41b918c9 (io-compression-zip, security-cryptography-random, storage, text-regular-expressions); io-isolated-storage gained tests.
concepts.note: Bible: five untested directories and 36 + 1 executables.

concepts.section: Tests enforce component ownership
concepts.text: text-regular-expressions is a 12-header INTERFACE component whose Regex is implemented inline over std::regex (ECMAScript), covered only by integration parity tests.
concepts.note: Bible: no implementation and no tests.

concepts.section: Tests enforce component ownership
concepts.text: A negative consumer fixture succeeds when the forbidden dependency fails to compile or link; treating every non-zero exit as a CI failure would invert it.

concepts.section: Upgrade rules for the seam
concepts.text: Upgrade procedure: record both revisions, use CNA_SHARP_RUNTIME_ROOT, read the shape message, keep lists narrow, run the sibling's boundary gates then CNA's build with sibling tests off.

concepts.section: Upgrade rules for the seam
concepts.text: When the sibling is on main or develop, configure stops inside sharp-runtime's own CMake with 'Unknown Sharp Runtime component 'Resources'', before CNA's shape message, because CNA's closure names components only next has.

target.evidence: CMakeLists.txt (SHARP_RUNTIME_COMPONENTS before add_subdirectory); sharp-runtime main/develop cmake/SharpRuntimeComponents.cmake (sharp_runtime_enable_component)

concepts.note: Derived by reading both repositories; the configure was not executed.

concepts.section: Upgrade rules for the seam
concepts.text: A verification report must separate 'these components were configured' from 'this target links only its declared closure'; at TARGET the first is CNA's closure plus dependencies, not all components.

issues.text: CNA excludes Xml.Serialization (and XmlSerializationEXT support and tests) on Windows because of a <poll.h> include that sharp-runtime next already guarded (88c12f15, 2026-09-14).
CNA records no sharp-runtime pin; CI mixes branch clones with August pins that lack Resources/Xml.Serialization.
The sharp-runtime README still says 41 selectable components while its generated catalogue reports 44 physical modules (47 names) at 41b918c9.
sharp-runtime Regex is a header-only std::regex (ECMAScript) wrapper: .NET-only syntax is translated or stripped and match timeouts cannot interrupt a search.
